name: Bell-eel

baseline.name: Bell-eel
baseline.look: Long translucent eel with mineral-rimmed resonator chambers.
baseline.ecology: Hunts vibration in deep channels and nests in quiet rock pockets.
baseline.limit: Sound carries far through water; light alone does not repel it.
baseline.encounter: Reduce hull impacts, use known quiet passages and avoid nesting seasons.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: Bell-eels hunt vibrations in deep channels. Mineral-rimmed chambers resonate as the flexible body moves. Brightness may reveal position but does not frighten them away.
cycle: Nesting occurs in quiet rock pockets when local water conditions permit. Lumen Tide observers record the season by the channel, not by a surface calendar.
signs: A hull tap answered by a low water-borne ring suggests investigation. Suspended silt and chamber glints help locate movement; sound can travel from elsewhere.
escalation: Distant orienting -> parallel follow -> close investigation -> strike at a strong local stimulus. A quiet boat is less conspicuous, not magically invisible.
community: Navigators teach quiet handling and protect nesting charts. Rescue partners receive the route facts they need without automatic access to every protected pocket.
scene: Namu shares a narrow rescue chart and accepts a visitor’s correction to a sounding. Trust grows through usable, bounded information rather than surrender of the whole archive.
motion: Lock chamber number and spacing for each animal design; bend the body continuously. Do not generate disconnected glowing beads or growing extra fins.
sounds: Low resonances conducted through water and occasional surface ripples. No sonar that reads minds or understands messages.
rule: Blind channel hunter; seven-metre representative length, no light-repulsion shortcut and no tunnel to the Burrow.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
